sourcePolicy: Official ISM monthly reports and ISM's own report roundup are authoritative; aggregate diffusion data and ISM-selected public respondent comments only. No confidential/raw survey submissions are claimed or used.

releaseStatus.note: Both August 2026 Manufacturing and Services reports are now published and incorporated.

industries.largeIndustryRead: Five of the six largest industries expanded: Transportation Equipment, Petroleum & Coal Products, Computer & Electronic Products, Machinery, and Food/Beverage/Tobacco.

themes: AI infrastructure demand is contributing to severe electronics/component and material constraints.
Machinery respondents cited energy, steel and labor cost increases while photonics, high-speed connectors, semiconductors and government-related demand remained strong.
Chemical-product comments linked tariffs/Hormuz inflation to customer purchasing-power risk.
Pricing volatility, Iran conflict, lead times and tariffs were prominent negative-comment drivers.

manufacturing.powerStackInterpretation: Production remains strong and customers' inventories remain too low, but New Orders/Backlog/Employment slowed. Prices at 71.1, slower supplier deliveries and explicit copper/electrical/electronic/memory/wire scarcity support real physical bottlenecks. Prefer booked orders/pricing power over speculative capacity plans.

prices.note: Highest since October 2022 / near four-year high.

customersInventories.note: Services report does not publish a Customers' Inventories index; no value inferred.

commodities.note: ISM reported fewer commodities with broad price changes than July, but petroleum products remained up and GPUs/steel joined the short-supply list; memory remained short for an eighth month.

respondentCommentReview.scope: ISM-selected public comments / ISM roundup only.
themes: Large capital investment in transmission and generation services is increasing business activity, head count, material purchasing and long-lead planning.
Suppliers are reallocating capacity from current-generation components toward upcoming next-generation AI silicon/platforms, which can lengthen lead times for legacy parts.
Companies are building inventories for long-lead items and 2027 projects.
Hiring remains restrained despite strong business activity; firms are leaving positions open longer and using fewer workers where service levels permit.
Tariffs and Middle East conflict remain important supply-chain and price concerns.

services.powerStackInterpretation: This is a materially stronger demand signal than July, but it is not benign growth. Orders/activity/backlogs accelerated while employment remained in contraction and Prices jumped to 72.6. For Power Stack, the highest-value evidence is explicit transmission/generation long-lead purchasing and AI component capacity reallocation. This supports ETN/PWR/GEV/VRT and scarce AI components, while high borrowing/input costs still penalize long-duration and unfunded projects.

combinedRead: August Manufacturing and Services now show a bifurcated stagflationary expansion: physical production/services demand remain solid, services orders reaccelerated sharply, and electrical/AI/transmission scarcity is real; at the same time, input-price pressure is extreme and hiring is weak. The correct Power Stack response is quality selection, pricing power, real backlog and funded demand, not blanket cyclical or AI beta.
rawSubmissionNote: ISM publishes selected comments and aggregate diffusion data, not the confidential individual survey submission database.
